page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-48 is a compute-focused server instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 180 GB of RAM. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, supported by dedicated CPU allocation. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 260 MB L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-48 demonstrates strong performance in compute-heavy tasks. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2175.0 and a multi-core score of 18084.0, both falling into the top 25% tier. Its image processing and text processing capabilities are highly rated, reaching the top 10% tier. The instance also shows strong performance in software compilation, scoring 41506.0 on Geekbench, and ray tracing at 53882.0. Cryptographic and mathematical operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to a Passmark CPU score of 54598.51.

The memory subsystem provides 180 GB of RAM, translating to 3.75 GB per core. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only speed of 144.84 GB/sec for large uncached blocks and 3389.0 GB/sec for cached small blocks. The instance lacks local NVMe storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. This server is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, image and text processing, static web serving, and moderate large language model inference tasks.
